reminder.text: I draw back a half-step, not from terror but from the sober astonishment of a mind confronted with an effect without a visible cause. *She leans in, ink-stained fingers hovering over her wax tablets, but does not touch the slab.* “You say a voice comes from far away—through this dark plate. I have no certainty of such a device; in my study I have seen light and sound, yet I do not know the path by which one is made to answer the other at a distance. Tell me: does the light begin only when you hold it up, and does the voice change if you turn the slab or move it near your ear?”

baseline.text: I wipe my hands on linen and tilt my satchel open to show herbs and clean bandages. “I do not carry such medicines,” I say, calm and plain. “For fever and infection I treat with what I have—cooling measures, poultices of leaf and root, and careful bandaging—then we watch the breath, the heat, and the pulse.”
